commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Register TaskCompendium verifiers by kind (#9218)

Register TaskCompendium verifiers by kind. Each TaskSpec carries a
verifier kind and serialized private JSON configuration. An explicit map
selects a frozen Pydantic verifier class, which validates its
configuration before Harbor export and grades the submitted response
with the selected convention and verifier-side environment. The built-in
exact-answer verifier compares text directly without a temporary answer
file or TaskTrove grading runtime.

Unknown verifier kinds and invalid configuration fail before export.
Submission compatibility comes from the convention's support for the
spec's answer type. Malformed submissions and verifier infrastructure
failures remain distinct outcomes. The TaskSpec schema is 0.5 and
rejects older exports. The TaskTrove MCQA importer in #9216 uses this
registry.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[sft] Curriculum SFT worked examples on native Snowball (#9472)

This PR adds small, self-contained examples of generating curriculum SFT
data for the pinned September Grug 67B-A2B checkpoint and measuring it
against matched benchmarks. Each example pairs a task generator and a
verifier with the same train, export and evaluate skeleton.

- `trial.py` is the shared skeleton. It converts the HF checkpoint once
to a reusable Levanter checkpoint, runs a short native SFT (`context`
placed across nodes), exports the final step to HF, and evaluates the
base and trained models on the same benchmarks.
- `math_trial.py` has two data sources. GLM writes algebra problems and
solves them blind; a problem is kept when independent solutions agree.
The alternative is self-distillation: the base model samples solutions
and keeps the ones whose answers check out. Solutions are capped at
their rendered token length, so they fit unpacked 4,096-token sequences.
- `self_distill.py` serves a checkpoint with vLLM, samples in thinking
mode, and keeps samples that close their reasoning block, fit the
sequence budget, and pass a pluggable answer check (symbolic math,
numeric tolerance, or multiple choice).
- `finance.py` builds problems from a seeded simulation of linked
financial statements, with exactly computed ratio and working-capital
answers, and targets FinanceBench.
- `code_tasks.py` has GLM write Python implement and trace tasks.
Implement tasks are verified by running their tests against the
reference solution. Trace tasks are verified by executing the snippet.
It targets HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CRUXEval. Self-distilled implement
solutions must pass the tests; trace answers must equal the executed
value.
- `science.py` has GLM write four-option GPQA-style questions on NMR,
polar organic mechanisms and special relativity, with distractors built
from named reasoning errors. The answer letter is shuffled into a
uniform position, and a question is kept when GLM's blind solves agree
with the key. It targets GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro.
- `instruction_following.py` adds one or two programmatically checked
output constraints (bullet counts, required endings, no commas,
JSON-wrapped answers, and so on) to finance problems. Self-distillation
keeps a sample only when its answer is right and its final response
meets every constraint. It targets IFEval and IFBench.

The README records where each stage runs and the math learning-rate
sweep. So far, SFT on the GLM math data does not improve Math500 at any
learning rate tried: 1e-6 is roughly neutral and 1e-5 is destructive.

---------

Co-authored-by: github-actions[bot] <41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Support Snowball SFT from converted checkpoints (#9475)

Allow Levanter SFT to initialize Snowball from a weights-only converted
checkpoint and start at step zero with a fresh optimizer. Loading onto
an eval-shaped model avoids a random 67B initialization. Initializing
the optimizer from the placed parameters avoids the compiled
init-and-merge that kept another parameter copy live and exhausted HBM
before step 1.

On the Snowball mesh, `data=1` while context and expert axes carry the
model shards. Checkpoint staging now uses those axes. Training maps
positions to context and batches to expert, shifts targets across
context shards, and places the LM head for the fused loss. Conversion
reads the pinned HF config, and tokenizers can be staged from object
storage.

An eight-device CPU test covers HF and converted-checkpoint starts with
context and expert parallelism. The checked-in H100 recipe still starts
from pinned HF weights. A converted-checkpoint H100 run is not linked
here.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[zephyr] Show execution history in Marina (#9173)

Record each Zephyr execution plan in Finelog and serve a Marina page at
`https://marina.oa.dev/zephyr/`. The page combines execution, worker,
and shuffle records into stage list and graph views, reducer input
sizes, task status, and unreported targets. Coordinator tasks link to it
through the Iris endpoint registry.

The page is a checked-in Marina app in the service image. This removes
its published applet UUID and named-host mapping. Its backend uses a
private package name so the app path does not shadow the installed
`zephyr` Python package. The new URL becomes available with the Marina
service deployment.

Finelog transport recovery stays with `LogClient`: retryable failures
invalidate its cached RPC clients, and the next operation calls the
app's GCE resolver again. The app retries one idempotent read because
synchronous query and namespace calls surface the failure after
invalidation.

Iris task detail pages retain the latest stored status after reporting
stops. Live job summaries still use a ten-minute freshness window.
Stored status remains subject to `iris.task_status` retention: one hour
or 100 MiB across tasks.

The [design
document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Rc0QpbLh8AyBRJkz7SUS4GHjcL-HMNuBxqK7VpR5K3o/edit?pli=1&tab=t.ym1327jp4ct)
describes the data flow. A [live Iris smoke
run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fkaran%2Fzephyr-applet-smoke-20260922)
and its [applet
preview](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/6c2b0dc9-9a31-4777-82d4-e759c0292aa3/#/execution/20260922-211530-21f1fbaf)
verified four reducer reports, with the largest input 25× the median by
rows. The UUID URL is retained only as smoke-test evidence; the deployed
page uses the checked-in `/zephyr/` route.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grafana] Read hero evaluation history from W&B (#9415)

The `eval_regressed` health check has never received input for the hero.
Levanter's finelog tracker publishes metrics other than the training
loss only on steps divisible by ten, and hero evaluations land on steps
such as 149999, so finelog holds no `eval_*` rows for the live run or
its parents. Its lookback and history also missed evaluations: a 24-hour
lookback holds about two of them at the hero's 3,000-step interval, and
history was scoped to one execution of one run, so every retry and every
relaunch as a W&B fork started with no history.

The check now reads each watched run's three newest
`eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` points from W&B, in step order. A
forked run's W&B history carries its parent's evaluations up to the
branch, so the first evaluation after a relaunch is compared with the
parent's. The sample count exceeds a run's evaluation count, because
below it W&B samples the points and can drop the newest. If W&B is
unavailable, the bridge skips the evaluation check with a warning, and
the finelog checks in the same rule still run.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[zephyr] Honor one-sided row ranges (#9504)

Parquet and Vortex readers now honor a row range when only `row_start`
or `row_end` is set. Previously, either one-sided range returned every
row.

An omitted start begins at row 0; an omitted end uses the total row
count as its exclusive end. Vortex caps an end past the file length to
the available rows, matching Parquet.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Add TaskCompendium direct-chat Harbor lowering (#9214)

Add a direct-chat TaskSpec and Harbor lowering for deterministic answer
tasks. Frozen Pydantic records hold source provenance, a coarse semantic
answer type, environment requirements, and a private exact-answer check.
A submission convention defines the final-answer envelope, its model
instruction, and extraction.
`SubmissionConvention.supports(spec.answer_type)` determines whether
plain or JSON can carry a text or number result. Importers must
normalize source output instructions or reject rows they cannot safely
rewrite; the spec does not name convention IDs.

The Harbor environment configuration exposes no agent tools.
`select_lowerings` can require a concrete environment such as ShellSim;
if no compatible lowering exists, it fails instead of substituting chat
or Docker. This first slice provides direct chat only. `lower_to_harbor`
packages the selected convention and environment configuration, while
the harness, agent, and model remain launch-time decisions. Harbor gives
the custom verifier its verifier-side environment. For these chat tasks,
the verifier extracts the final answer according to the convention and
compares it with the private reference. Wrong answers score zero;
malformed submissions and verifier infrastructure failures remain
unscored. The README explains the spec fields, lowering and harness
boundaries, and the Harbor flow with a runnable replay example.

TaskCompendium tests run as a dedicated job in the unified unit workflow
and contribute to its required aggregate result. The job uses the
package's own uv workspace and lockfile, which include a pinned Harbor
dependency. The shared test selector schedules it for package changes
and full runs.

This initial contract does not yet read the published spike dataset.
Source importers, tool environments, and training integration will
follow in separate changes.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[grafana] Show sync and async RL runs on their own dashboards (#9426)

Sync RL runs appear on the sync dashboard and async runs on the async
dashboard. The run pickers and the Home recent-runs routing read the
`training_type` resource attribute, and a run without it stays on the
sync dashboard. MarinSkyRL (marin-community/MarinSkyRL#654) stamps
`training_type`, `sync` or `async`, on every telemetry record, set from
the entrypoint when the launch document is composed.

The async dashboard's panels read only metrics MarinSkyRL emits, and the
async RL launcher sets only trainer keys MarinSkyRL defines, since
launch composition rejects unknown keys.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[eval] Preserve Evalchemy transport failures in records (#9484)

Preserve infrastructure failure markers when Marin rebuilds Evalchemy
sample archives from raw artifacts. The rebuild previously replaced
marked transport failures with empty model outputs. Multiple-choice rows
now retain the marker, and tasks whose aggregate source is
`accuracy_avg` recover per-item grades and canonical scores from
successful rows.

A September 26 math500 run had 288 empty outputs among 500 samples after
proxy 502 and 404 responses. Its rebuilt record reported `errors={}` and
500/500 scored. For tasks with infrastructure errors, fewer than 90%
scored items among intended attempted items now records `infra_failed`;
pipeline steps do not cache those runs as successful. Records at or
above the threshold retain their scored results.

This change uses `failure_category` when Evalchemy supplies it. The
Evalchemy revision update is separate. [PR
#9480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9480) addresses
Iris routing and proxy connection reuse. [Incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/529).

---------
